Code and Theory is looking for a Multi-Solution Architect to lead commerce architecture within our Adobe practice, anchoring the Adobe Commerce pillar alongside our AEM, Workfront, and AEP/data practices.

You'll play a vital role in the architecture, design, configuration, testing, and deployment of Adobe Commerce solutions and the Adobe Experience Cloud platforms around them, including Experience Platform, Real-Time CDP, Experience Manager, Edge Delivery Services, Target, and Workfront.

Working closely with Engineering, Strategy, and Sales teams and directly with clients, you'll provide best-fit architecture for commerce programs, help define scope and sizing, anchor proof-of-concept builds, and design integrations with ERP, OMS, PIM, and other third-party services.

What You'll Do

 Architect end-to-end Adobe Commerce (Magento Open Source and Commerce/Cloud) solutions for enterprise B2B and B2C clients, from catalog and pricing to checkout, order management, and fulfillment. Design headless and composable commerce architectures using PWA Studio, Adobe Commerce Storefront, GraphQL, and API-first integration patterns. Collaborative mindset and the ability to work across creative, data, content, and engineering teams on integrated solutions.

Multi-solution architecture experience across other Adobe products (AEM, AEP, Workfront) in addition to Commerce. Job Description

About the Role

We are building an in-house team to maintain and contribute to our internal Apache Kafka distribution. This is not an operations role — you will work on the Kafka codebase itself: the broker, the KRaft controller, the protocol, the clients, and the storage layer. You will be our technical anchor for all things Kafka internals, driving upstream contributions, backporting critical fixes, and shaping our internal distribution to meet the needs of a large-scale production fleet.

We already do this successfully with GlusterFS, where we maintain an in-house distribution backed by deep upstream expertise. We want to replicate that model for Kafka.

Key Responsibilities

Own our internal Kafka distribution: branch management, patch curation, release cutting, upgrade planningContribute upstream to Apache Kafka — bug fixes, KIPs, code reviews, design discussionsDiagnose and fix deep broker/controller issues: replication, partition reassignment, KRaft consensus, log storage, ISR management, protocol handlingBuild custom patches for production needs that aren't suitable for upstream (performance tuning for our workload profile, observability hooks, operational safety valves)Establish engineering practices for Kafka development within the team: how we test, how we benchmark, how we validate patches before rolling them outMentor a supporting engineer and grow the team's capability over timeAct as the internal authority on Kafka internals — advise platform teams on configuration, capacity planning, and architectural decisions that require knowledge of broker behaviorAct as the primary interface for audit and compliance teams, ensuring PhonePe Kafka distribution meets various compliance and regulatory standards

Qualifications

What are we looking for?

Deep familiarity with the Kafka codebase — you have read, modified, and debugged the broker, controller, or client internals. Not just operated Kafka, but worked on it. Track record of upstream contribution — committed patches, participated in KIP discussions, reviewed PRs, or equivalent engagement with the Apache Kafka community. Active committer/PMC status is strongly preferred but not strictly required if your contribution history demonstrates equivalent depth. Strong distributed systems fundamentals — consensus protocols, replication, exactly-once semantics, log-structured storage, distributed state machines. You understand these not as buzzwords but as engineering tradeoffs you've navigated. Systems-level programming comfort — JVM internals (GC tuning, memory layout, JIT behavior), OS-level I/O (page cache, fsync semantics, zero-copy), networking (TCP tuning, socket buffers). Kafka performance work lives at this layer. Experience maintaining a fork or distribution — you've managed the tension between carrying local patches and staying mergeable with upstream. You know what it costs to diverge and how to minimize that cost. 8+ years of experience in systems/infrastructure software engineering, with a meaningful portion spent on Kafka or comparable distributed systems (Pulsar, Bookkeeper, Zookeeper, etcd, CockroachDB, etc.)

Additional Information

About Agent Studio

Agent Studio helps Razorpay merchants run AI agents across payments, checkout, disputes, subscriptions, reconciliation, risk, and customer workflows. We take the messy, undocumented work merchants do every day and turn it into reliable production agents.

The role

We're hiring a Forward-Deployed Engineer who is equal parts engineer, solution consultant, and merchant partner — the single technical owner of the merchant relationship. You'll sit directly with strategic merchants, run the discovery, find the real constraint behind the ask, design the solution, build the first working version, prove whether it moved the metric, and expand from there.

This is a deeply customer-facing role. You'll own the conversation — not hand it off. You'll walk into a room where the business owner, the ops lead, and the dashboard all tell different stories, and you'll be the one who reconciles them into a spec everyone agrees to ship. Then you'll go build it. You earn the customer's trust because you can do both — reshape the ask and write the code.

If you like being close to the problem, comfortable in front of customers, and can ship, this is for you.

What You'll Own

Customer discovery & the relationship

Own merchant conversations end-to-end — discovery calls, workshops, solution reviews, and rollout check-ins. You're the merchant's trusted technical advisor.Sit inside merchant workflows long enough to understand the real process, not the documented one. Ask who actually does the work and what happens when it fails.Reconcile conflicting signals across business owners, operators, dashboards, CRM, and ticket queues into a clear problem statement.


Solution design & consulting

Name the business constraint behind the ask: checkout recovery, dispute win rate, RTO loss, SIP recovery, settlement delay, refund spikes, support load, or cashflow leakage.Convert fuzzy merchant problems into crisp agent specs: success metric, data sources, tool calls, guardrails, human-in-the-loop points, and rollout plan.Decide what the agent does on its own, what it recommends, and where a human must approve.Write the spec clearly enough that product, engineering, legal, and the merchant all agree on what ships.


Hands-on build & integration

Build prototypes, connectors, MCP tool specs, eval fixtures, dashboards, and the glue code that gets an agent into production.Debug integration failures across Razorpay systems, merchant systems, external tools, and model behavior.Deploy across the constraints that real merchants have — auth, networking, data access, latency, cost per run, observability, and compliance — and keep them in the design from day one.


Proof, expansion & productization

Set quality gates and outcome metrics before rollout. Track production outcomes, not demo applause.Measure whether the agent moved the target metric. If it didn't, diagnose and fix — or kill it with evidence.Drive expansion through building: spot the next high-value use case, prototype it, and deepen the merchant's agent footprint over time.Turn repeated field patterns into reusable Agent Studio capabilities — connectors, templates, eval packs, docs, platform requirements. You are the field voice that shapes what the platform builds next.


You may be a fit if you

Have 3+ years shipping production software, and are strong in Python or TypeScript.Have worked directly with customers, enterprise stakeholders, or operators — and are comfortable owning the room and the technical relationship.Have hands-on experience with APIs, webhooks, auth, data pipelines, and production debugging.Have practical LLM/agent experience: prompts, tool calling, RAG, evals, or workflow automation.Prefer ambiguous, high-context problems over clean tickets.Take ambiguous problems, define the structure, and drive them to resolution Write clearly — specs, implementation plans, and crisp follow-ups.
